claims.qualification: For US-DFC_1_000, source rows 902 and 904 both report 1.0471285 MPa, with water contents 19.12% and 12.21%. Retain both; no averaging or correction is inferred.

context: Reported water content (%) is the source column Vol_Water. The available metadata says “Sample Water Content (%)” without explicitly defining volume/volume. This page does not convert those measurements into storage.

Water-potential magnitude, MPa, displays the positive source MPa_Abs values. The metadata describes negative water potential; the chart shows magnitude, not positive signed potential. MPa is a pressure unit.

The chart spaces magnitudes using log10: equal distances represent equal ratios. Raw magnitudes remain available in the point readout and full tables. Points are unconnected; repeated x values remain separate observations.
Hypropfilter is an instrument code: 1 = WP4C; 2 = HyProp. It is not a quality flag. No calibration or measurement-uncertainty audit is claimed.
Density is omitted because its documented units conflict with the values. Conductivity is omitted; its caution flags do not constitute a blanket rating of retention rows.

The local audit uses frozen original metadata and hash-matched CSVs. The later API check was inaccessible, so no fresh remote verification is claimed. Soil-science unit interpretation and representative sampling remain open publication questions.

What does a soil-water point measure?

Follow an observation from a source row to a plot—and keep assumptions separate.

Explore 278 laboratory observations from three samples in one plot at Prairie du Sac, Wisconsin. Compare raw points, inspect instrument labels, and try a separate synthetic storage calculation.

Local review covers source fidelity, evidence labeling and bounded prototype reuse. No professional specialist, screen-reader or learner session has been performed.

A descriptive single-plot subset, not a controlled depth experiment, fitted retention curve or irrigation recommendation.

  1. Read the sources
  2. Explore the evidence
  3. Explain a limitation
01

Read closely

Ankur Desai, Alison Duff, Susanne Wiesner, Emily Mather, Jonathan Thom, Daniel Beverly, Alex Crookshanks, Trevor Gress, Max Crookshanks

The unit of observation

Original explanation

A row records a reported water-content value and water-potential magnitude for a named sample and instrument. A sample contributes many such rows.

Editorial context: Original explanation based on the pinned CSV and its metadata. The full file has 1,106 rows from 12 samples; this page retains all 278 rows from the three reported depths in plot 1. These are not 278 independent field samples.

Source and reuse details

ReESH_US-DFC: US Dairy Forage Research Center, Prairie du Sac

Record 18273606; US_DFC_SoilWaterRetentionCurves.csv, all plot 1 rows · Sampled 2025-05-29; record publication 2026-01-16; API created/modified 2026-03-03

The inspected metadata declares CC BY 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Creators, title, version DOI and modifications are attributed here.

Selected all three plot 1 samples, projected eight columns, preserved decimal strings and row order. Plot x positions use log10; values and tables remain raw. No fitted data or imported figures.

What this exploration can establish

  • Reported water content (%) is the source column Vol_Water. The available metadata says “Sample Water Content (%)” without explicitly defining volume/volume. This page does not convert those measurements into storage.
  • Water-potential magnitude, MPa, displays the positive source MPa_Abs values. The metadata describes negative water potential; the chart shows magnitude, not positive signed potential. MPa is a pressure unit.
  • The chart spaces magnitudes using log10: equal distances represent equal ratios. Raw magnitudes remain available in the point readout and full tables. Points are unconnected; repeated x values remain separate observations.
  • Hypropfilter is an instrument code: 1 = WP4C; 2 = HyProp. It is not a quality flag. No calibration or measurement-uncertainty audit is claimed.
  • Density is omitted because its documented units conflict with the values. Conductivity is omitted; its caution flags do not constitute a blanket rating of retention rows.
  • The local audit uses frozen original metadata and hash-matched CSVs. The later API check was inaccessible, so no fresh remote verification is claimed. Soil-science unit interpretation and representative sampling remain open publication questions.
02

All observed retention rows from the three reported depths in plot 1; illustrative within one plot, not a representative site sample or controlled experiment.

Data: Desai, Duff, Wiesner, Mather, Thom, Beverly, A. Crookshanks, Gress and M. Crookshanks. ReESH_US-DFC, record 18273606, CC BY 4.0. Changes: all plot 1 rows selected, eight columns projected, x coordinates log10 transformed; no measured values altered.

File: US_DFC_SoilWaterRetentionCurves.csv. SHA-256: 41308fba78d50d96152f40b85af43f45a9aed4d53e23568db483889c8ed744b1.

Excluded columns: Latitude, Longitude, Veg, Bulk_Den_g_m3. Reproduction script verifies the pinned file before comparing the complete projection with this page’s record.

A separate synthetic model

Assume a uniform layer with upper volumetric fraction 0.30, lower fraction 0.15 and depth 0.40 m. Storage difference = (0.30 − 0.15) × 0.40 × 1000 = 60 mm. The 1000 converts metres to millimetres.

These are invented model parameters, not measured thresholds, field capacity, wilting point or an irrigation instruction. Changing them does not alter the observed points.

One notebook for this exploration revision, up to 1,500 characters. Notes stay in this browser. Shared links contain selections only. Nothing is sent to a server.

03

Try the idea elsewhere

Choose two observed rows and describe exactly what differs. Then explain why neither a difference between depths nor the synthetic 60 mm example tells a farmer when to irrigate.

What a careful explanation includes
  • Name sample, source row, instrument, units and the observed values.
  • Distinguish row count from independent sample count, and an x-axis transformation from a new measurement.
  • Keep repeated magnitudes and their distinct observations visible.
  • State the synthetic fractions, uniform layer and metre-to-millimetre conversion separately from the dataset.
  • Identify missing information before applying a result to another site or crop.

There is no automatic score for your written interpretation. Use the guide to inspect your reasoning.

These decisions apply only to the exact digests below, original numerical observations plus original explanations, and the declared local-preview scope. Independent soil-science interpretation and representative-sampling questions remain explicitly open for publication. This receipt does not approve a public release or satisfy an unrelated professional/human review requirement.

## Measurement fidelity

Independently parsed the supplied HTML tables with Python HTMLParser and compared every source row, magnitude string, water string and instrument label against the original CSV projection. **All278 rendered table rows match exactly.** Evidence `/tmp/atlas-p05-artifact-rowchecks.json`.

"""Verify the complete pilot projection against the pinned original local CSV.
Usage: python3 docs/pilots/research/soil-subset.py /path/to/original/csv/directory
No network or writes; source decimals, order and duplicate magnitudes are preserved.
"""
import csv
import hashlib
import io
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
record = json.loads((ROOT / 'explorations/agriculture.json').read_text())
dataset = record['activity']['dataset']
raw = (Path(sys.argv[1]) / dataset['sourceFile']).read_bytes()
expected = '41308fba78d50d96152f40b85af43f45a9aed4d53e23568db483889c8ed744b1'
if hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() != expected or dataset['sourceSha256'] != expected:
    raise ValueError('Original CSV hash mismatch; review another edition explicitly')
columns = ['Site','Sample_ID','Plot','Depth_cm','MPa_Abs','Vol_Water','Hypropfilter','Sampling_Date']
samples = ['US-DFC_1_000','US-DFC_1_010','US-DFC_1_050']
rows = [dict(sourceRow=i, **{k:r[k] for k in columns})
        for i,r in enumerate(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(raw.decode('utf-8'))), start=2)
        if r['Sample_ID'] in samples]
if dataset['selection']['Sample_ID'] != samples or dataset['projection'] != columns or dataset['rows'] != rows:
    raise ValueError('Projection differs from every retained source row, value or source order')
print(json.dumps({'verifiedRows':len(rows),'samples':{s:sum(r['Sample_ID']==s for r in rows) for s in samples},'originalSha256':expected}))
